note:
THE MOLECULE CHECK DECIDED BOTH PICKS, AND IT OVERTURNED THE ONE THAT LOOKED BEST.

nbp_pro_01 won the approach block on the contact sheet and on the render-size pairing — closest palette to the live Matrixyl set, cleanest block geometry, best match to the chosen causes frame. At 100% it fails twice: its copper chains carry FIVE beads, not three, and its bead ladders visibly SPIRAL. GHK-Cu is a TRIpeptide, so five beads is not a styling preference, it is the wrong molecule; and a spiralling ladder is the DNA-double-helix cliché the whole explainer set has negated from the start. Neither fault is visible below about 40% zoom.

So every one of the eleven candidates was cropped to its sphere band at full resolution and the beads counted. On the count: gpt-image (both), nbp_flash (both), nbp_pro_02, seedream (both) and luma_01 all render the tripeptide correctly as pearl-copper-pearl; nbp_pro_01 and luma_02 do not; FLUX.2 adds GOLD beads alongside the copper, which is negated by name. That is the same lesson as the shipping-box helix, one level further in — a chain that reads right at thumbnail size can be the wrong molecule at full size, and only counting finds it.

Of the candidates that survive the count, nbp_flash_02 is the best picture: four spheres, two ladders and two tripeptides, shafts of light rather than the solid copper RODS nbp_pro_02 rendered, and a soft high-key palette that sits with the Matrixyl set instead of gpt-image's saturated blue wall.

causes  keeps nbp_pro_01 — it is a different slot and its faults were all in the sphere band, which that frame does not have. Verified at 100%: piled lifting plates, grey specks settling into the hollows, cell rows thinned to a sparse row, the surface sagging into a broad furrow over an empty gap, sparse slack fibre, and NO spheres, shafts or glints anywhere.
